Popup Analytics

An analysis of how luxury cosmetics pop-up stores performed across regions and event formats, presented as a Power BI dashboard for executives.

Overview

Luxury cosmetics brands run short pop-up stores in malls, airports and event venues. The question behind this project was practical: which locations and event formats actually pay off? I analysed sales, footfall, pricing and duration across regions and turned the answers into a Power BI dashboard for executives.

Headline numbers

  • 398.74M total revenue across the events in the dataset, from 4M units sold.
  • 186.94K average revenue per event.
  • 73.37% average sell-through — most stock placed in a pop-up actually sells.
  • 2.93% conversion rate, measured against footfall.

What I found

The most useful result was that footfall and revenue do not move together. Ranking event formats by revenue per day against average daily footfall separates them clearly:

  • Flash Events earn the most per day (~4.2K) on some of the lowest footfall — short, concentrated events convert best.
  • Mall Kiosks draw the highest footfall but earn the least per day, so traffic alone is a poor target.
  • By location type, Art/Design District leads on revenue per day (4.5K) ahead of Luxury Mall (3.7K).
  • Revenue is spread evenly across regions — Europe leads at 89M, Asia-Pacific trails at 73M — so the opportunity is in format, not geography.

Deliverable

An executive-ready Power BI dashboard: KPI cards across the top, then brand, region, location-type and event-format breakdowns, plus a monthly revenue trend with a date slicer. The trend page carries a note that the final months are incomplete, so the drop at the end is not read as falling sales.
